title: Descent component of the canonical pullback compositor
statement:
theorem tensorComparison_composition_descent {X Y Z : Site.{u, w}}
    (f : RingedPullback.{u, u, u, u, u} Z.A Y.A)
    (g : RingedPullback.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.A X.A)
    (h : RingedPullback.{u, u, u, u, u} Z.A X.A)
    (kf : CochainPullback.Comparison.{u, u, u, u, u} f) (kg : CochainPullback.Comparison.{u, u, u,
      u, u} g) (kh : CochainPullback.Comparison.{u, u, u, u, u} h)
    (a : CochainPullback.CompositePresentation.{u, u, u, u, u, u, u} f g h kf kg kh)
    (df : Pullback.{u, w} f) (dg : Pullback.{u, w} g) (dh : Pullback.{u, w} h) :
        ∃! c : dh.F ≅ df.F ⋙ dg.F,
      (∀ (P : CochainPullback.Complex.{u, u, u} Z.A), Resolving Z P →
        c.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫ dg.F.map (df.epsilon.app P) ≫
            dg.epsilon.app ((CochainPullback.pull.{u, u, u, u, u} f).obj P) =
          dh.epsilon.app P ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainPullback.composition.{u, u, u, u, u, u,
            u} f g h a P).hom)

proof.text: Compose the actual derived counits for f and g. On every flat-term K-flat P, the first counit is invertible by resolving computation, and pullback preservation makes the second counit invertible as well. The same computation applies to h. The identical cochain natural isomorphism is now packaged as cochain_compositor in lem-pur-finite-tensor-comparison-proof-support, with its original component formula.

Use flat-term K-flat resolutions, converting the native tensor-flat condition to site flatness. Apply comparison_descent_iso to the ordinary cochain compositor and the two computed counits. Its unique normalized isomorphism is exactly the displayed compositor.
